name: Obsidian
tagline: Private, extensible knowledge base with linked notes and graph view

pricing.notes: Free for personal use; Sync ($5/mo) and Publish ($10/mo) are optional add-ons

verdictSummary: You can build a local markdown editor with a graph view in one sitting. But replacing Obsidian means replacing 2,000+ community plugins, the Canvas feature, live preview, and years of plugin ecosystem polish. The editor itself is not the moat — the plugin architecture is.
coreLoopDIY: Local markdown editor with bidirectional linking and graph visualization
moatNotes: The plugin ecosystem is 10 years of community investment — impossible to replicate in a one-shot
whyPeopleStillPay: Sync and Publish for sharing knowledge bases, or just the plugin ecosystem convenience
notes: Building a markdown wiki is easy. Building the plugin ecosystem is not.
